name: IN-02
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Rudy Yakym running with a large fundraising edge ($5.2M raised)
No polling and no expert ratings; prediction markets price Democratic chances near 4%
model.rationale: The district's R+13 lean, Yakym's incumbency and dominant fundraising, and markets pricing Democratic odds around 4% all point to a comfortable Republican hold, with no polling evidence suggesting a competitive race.
model.watch: A major late scandal or unexpectedly strong Democratic spending could narrow the margin, though nothing in the current evidence suggests that.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern Indiana's second district is solidly Republican territory, and incumbent Rudy Yakym is seeking another term after easily securing his party's nomination. Jamee Decio has raised a modest sum for the Democratic side, but Yakym has vastly outpaced her financially, with more than five million dollars raised and a cash advantage heading into the fall.

No public polling covers this race and no major expert raters have flagged it as competitive, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets give Democrats only a small chance of an upset. A Libertarian candidate, William Henry, is also on the ballot. The seat remains firmly in Republican hands barring an unforeseen development.
